questions: Is slalom line_loss_events 0 at ±0.08 m spread with y=0.07 m? If not, report the max_error at the first loss.
Is slalom max_error below 0.06 m? Report it per track.
Does s-bend progress stay near 0.18 and s-bend line_loss_events stay near 0?
Does steering_oscillation stay below about 0.13 on s-bend and slalom with the wider spread, or does the wider spread add jitter from lower resolution near centre?
Does the oval still stop at progress 0.115 with max_error near 0.061 m?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If slalom line loss is still 1 per run at ±0.08 m, the spread is not the slalom trigger, so keep the ±0.08 m spread and do not move the row. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.14 on s-bend or slalom with the wider spread, return to ±0.065 m and test the controller next rather than geometry. If the score is at or above 56.4 with zero line loss, test sensor_size 0.012 m at the same positions.

intent: Return the sensor row to y=0.07 m, the best-scoring lead (iteration 8, 56.40), and widen the sensor spread from ±0.065 m to ±0.08 m with 16 mm footprints. Change only the spread, so the result shows whether a wider spread removes the slalom line loss that persisted at ±0.065 m. Speed stays at wheel_radius 0.03 m, because 0.04 m caused line loss in iteration 6. The lead stays at 0.07 m, because 0.067 m lost s-bend progress in iteration 9.
learning: Iteration 9 showed the lead is sharply tuned: y=0.067 m cut s-bend progress and raised s-bend line loss to 0.5 per run, so y=0.07 m is the lead to keep. The spread is the lever that has reduced line loss in each step (±0.05 m to ±0.065 m cut s-bend line loss from 1 to 0.05 per run). This iteration tests whether the same lever reaches the remaining slalom loss at ±0.08 m.
rationale: Iteration 9 (y=0.067 m, ±0.065 m, 16 mm, 0.03 m speed) scored 51.11, below iteration 8 (y=0.07 m, same spread) at 56.40. The 3 mm lead cut was costly: s-bend line loss rose from 0.05 to 0.5 per run and s-bend progress fell from 0.1825 to 0.1474. Slalom still lost the line once per run, and its max_error worsened from 0.0604 to 0.0647 m. So y=0.067 m is worse on both bends, and I return the row to y=0.07 m, the best-scoring lead. Iteration 8's remaining fault is slalom: one line loss per run with max_error 0.0604 m and steering oscillation 0.131. Slalom oscillation has stayed at 0.13 to 0.14 at every row tested, so the row is not its cause. The wider spread did cut s-bend line loss from 1 to 0.05 per run (iteration 3 to 8), which shows that spread is the lever that keeps the tape in view on bends. Iteration 0 showed the line drops out of view at about 0.045 to 0.05 m offset with a narrow spread. The slalom loss at ±0.065 m is most likely the same effect at larger offsets. I therefore widen the spread to ±0.08 m (the contract maximum), keep the proven y=0.07 m lead, and keep 16 mm footprints, 0.03 m speed, 0.09 m track and 0.5 kg mass unchanged. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events near 0, slalom max_error below 0.06 m, s-bend progress around 0.18, and a score above 56.4. Risk: the wider spread lowers signal resolution near centre, which could add jitter or raise s-bend oscillation (0.127 in iteration 8).
